newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso extends gains, ending at 1,003.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso extends gains, ending at 1,003.

text.p: Colombia's peso extended its gains for the sixth consecutive day, ending up 4.1 at 1,003 despite central bank efforts to drive the buoyant local currency lower.
The closing rate was the lowest since Jan. 5, when the peso ended at 1,000 to the dollar.

Dealers said the central intervened aggressively in Wednesday's trading, buying about $25 million to halt the rise of the peso, which makes Colombian exports less attractive abroad and has prompted widespread concerns about the economy.

It was the second consecutive day that the central bank, or Banco de la Republica, intervened. But dealers said its dollar-buying was offset by heavy selling by banks and the mining sector and failed to halt the peso's sharp move upward.
Dealers reported 281 trades for a total of $111 million and said the peso held in a 1,002.80 to 1,004.70 range.
